canonical_name: Proxy ARP / Transparent Subnet Gateway technique (RFC 1027)

standardized.notes: RFC documents a technique described as already widely used.

roles: gateway answers ARP on behalf of remote hosts
hide subnet boundaries from hosts lacking subnet awareness
routing_or_forwarding: Gateway returns its own hardware address for a target on another physical network, then forwards received IP traffic by ordinary routing mechanisms.

operations.monitoring: Proxy ARP entries and gateway reachability affect host behavior.
operations.diagnostics: ARP replies appear to resolve a remote target to the gateway hardware address.
operations.failure_behavior: Can obscure topology and create surprising reachability/scale behavior when used broadly.
operations.operator_interface: Router configuration defaults/commands vary by vendor and release and remain to be catalogued.

open_questions: Recover University of Texas implementation described by RFC 1027.
Find earliest router-vendor proxy-ARP configuration manuals and defaults.
Trace operational deprecation/use cases without conflating Proxy ARP with NAT.

related_artifacts.notes: Technique uses ARP semantics rather than revising the base packet format.

notes: A canonical example of an installed-base compatibility mechanism: subnetting was useful before all connected hosts implemented subnet awareness.
